recent_posts.title: Scaling our invalidation pipeline: Part 2 • Asana
recent_posts.summary: Asana's platform engineering team tackled total load scalability and operational complexity in their invalidation pipeline. They addressed invalidation fanout issues through multiple approaches: attempting domain-isolated invalidations (which failed due to batching overhead), implementing invalidator replication per database as a stopgap, and ultimately migrating to a cell-based architecture for 10-20x fanout reduction. To reduce operational complexity from cache thrashing and binlog tailer issues, they're splitting the invalidator into separate generation and distribution components connected by an external datastore like Redis Streams or Kafka. Key lessons include biasing toward simplicity, validating core principles early, and recognizing the silent costs of maintaining complex generic systems.

recent_posts.title: Scaling our invalidation pipeline: Part 1 • Asana
recent_posts.summary: Asana's platform engineering team scaled their invalidation pipeline to handle near-realtime reactivity for millions of users. The pipeline uses change-data-capture from MySQL binlog to decouple mutations from invalidations, automatically determining affected data and notifying clients. The first major scaling challenge was expensive transactions causing head-of-line blocking. The solution involved introducing out-of-order invalidation delivery with a DataFreshness construct (similar to vector clocks) that maintains eventual consistency while allowing slow transactions to be processed asynchronously. This approach eliminated manual intervention and has worked successfully for 6 years without further optimization.

recent_posts.title: Stop Stuffing Prompts: How Asana Made Agents More Effective Through Context Engineering • Asana
recent_posts.summary: Asana developed an intent-augmented retrieval approach for AI systems that filters data based on user query intent before retrieval, rather than stuffing context windows with irrelevant information. Their context engineering strategy includes filtering at the field level, cross-encoder reranking, and intent-driven summarization, achieving 35% reduction in input tokens, 24% faster response times, and 30% lower costs while improving accuracy from 92-94% to 95-96%.

recent_posts.title: How Asana's Head of Engineering Sets Engineering Goals
recent_posts.summary: Asana's Head of Engineering emphasizes creating alignment through three types of clarity: purpose (why), plan (how), and responsibility (who/what). The company uses OKRs methodology with both bottom-up and top-down approaches, ensuring goals connect to daily execution rather than existing as isolated planning documents. Key advice includes involving development teams in goal-setting for better commitment, reframing engineering goals as business objectives, establishing measurable metrics upfront, and maintaining real-time visibility across departments for agile decision-making.

recent_posts.title: Meet our Security team - The Asana Blog
recent_posts.summary: Sean Cassidy, Asana's Head of Security, explains how the Security team protects customer data through vulnerability management, incident response, and AWS infrastructure security. The team uses Scala, Node, Python, and Rust for security tooling, implements MFA for SSH using MacBook secure enclaves, and leverages Asana extensively for tracking OKRs, risk registries, vulnerability management, and incident response workflows. The team prioritizes building a security-first culture across the entire company rather than operating in isolation.

top_posts.title: Scaling a Mature iOS Codebase with Tuist
top_posts.summary: Asana's Mobile Foundations team reduced iOS build times from 45 seconds to 15 seconds by migrating their 300,000-line Swift codebase to Tuist and splitting it into modules. The migration involved evaluating tools like Bazel and Swift Package Manager, ultimately choosing Tuist for its developer experience. Key challenges included migrating from CocoaPods, making thousands of symbols public, resolving circular dependencies using µFeatures architecture, and handling localization issues. The team created feature modules ranging from 5,000 to 30,000 lines of code, with AsanaCore now containing only 21% of the original codebase.

top_posts.title: Revamping engineering manager onboarding at Asana
top_posts.summary: Asana revamped their engineering manager onboarding process to address challenges with remote work and organizational growth. The new approach includes a structured 30-60-90 day plan template, multiple mentorship roles (technical, peer EM, cultural ambassador, and ERG mentors), cohort programs for different experience levels, and six onboarding tracks covering reports, team processes, dynamics, community building, technical aspects, and recruiting. Key learnings include making templates easily iterable, linking to existing resources rather than duplicating documentation, investing in mentor training, and ensuring clear milestone expectations from managers of managers.
